messages:
marta: heads-up — starting hybrid FP8+INT8 gguf export for starge-v2-13b. want a tight bring-up checklist and prioritization so we don't regress quality while chasing cost. low-risk path pls.

arjun: +1. do we have a baseline eval bundle and SLOs? what's the target cost reduction vs baseline fp16?

marta: baseline = hosted fp16-default. target is ~2.3x token-cost reduction with <=1.5% degradation on our core eval suite (answer F1 / instr-acc / embedding sim). latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms at sample traffic.

tess: propose a 3-stage plan: 1) smoke export + sanity metrics (ppl, empty-token checks) 2) calibration sweep (per-layer clipping, per-head scaling) on curated calibration set (1k prompts) 3) full eval (10k prompts, grading harness). Also add rollback triggers.

linh: calibration set note — include both short-chat and long-context prompts, and ~200 instruction-following examples where hallucination risk is higher. random-seed control is critical for comparison.

marta: agreed. quick checklist I'm going to follow: 
- export: gguf hybrid-fp8-int8 (per-layer dtype map)
- produce calibration artifacts and record all RNG seeds
- run smoke eval (100 prompts) against baseline and collect ppl, exact-match, embedding cosine
- run per-layer clipping sweep: clip=[0.99,0.995,0.999] and per-head-scale=[1.0,0.95,0.9]
- snapshot kernel perf: qps and p95
- if quality delta > 1.5% on any core metric OR hallucination rate increases > 0.5%, block rollout

arjun: small nit — include a tail-latency test under batching=8 and batching=32. sometimes quantization moves p95 tail. also note memory delta for Dedicated sizing.

marta: good call. adding tail-latency & mem checks.

tess: example export config (quick):
```
export_format: gguf
quant_scheme:
  - name: hybrid_fp8
    layers: embeddings,attn_qkv,mlp
    fallback: int8
    per_channel: true
    clip_method: percentile
    clip_threshold: 0.995
calibration_set: s3://redwood-evals/calib/starge-v2-13b/v1/
```

linh: for calibration runs use eval-harness v3 with flags: `--seed 42 --compare baseline --store-calib /tmp/calib.json` so we can reproduce exact numbers. also capture a tiny sample of failed outputs for manual review.

marta: QA gating rules i'm proposing: 
- smoke ppl delta <= 4%
- instr-acc delta <= 1.5% (primary)
- embedding-sim mean >= 0.98 of baseline
- hallucination examples reviewed if any automated hallucination detector score > 0.6
- p95 latency delta <= +15%
- memory <= baseline * 0.6 (for Dedicated binning)
if any rule fails, auto-mark as 'needs-tuning' and attach failing cases.

qa-bot: test-run queued: job id jr_8823. running smoke eval (100 prompts) now. will post results. :robot_face:

arjun: prioritization matrix idea — score candidate by: (quality_delta_weight=0.6, cost_saving_weight=0.3, infra_risk_weight=0.1). we should prefer smaller quality loss first and only accept high cost wins if quality holds.

marta: love that. for this model I'll set thresholds stricter (quality_weight cutoff 0.98 on instr-acc) and flag any head-scale < 0.9 as higher risk.

qa-bot: smoke results: ppl delta +1.8%, instr-acc delta -0.9%, embedding-sim 0.985, p95 latency +8%, memory -42%. storing calib at /artifacts/jr_8823/calib.json

tess: initial pass looks within our proposed gates. next step run calibration sweep with the clip thresholds and per-head scales. small-run first: 500 prompts.

marta: I'll kick sweep and post a matrix of (clip, head-scale) -> core metrics. we should pick the most cost-efficient point that meets all gates.

linh: note for rollout policy: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback to fp16 baseline if any new regression appears in live telemetry (accuracy or latency). also tag the model artifacts with the export config and eval hashes.

marta: perfect. thanks all — i'll open a PR with the checklist and attach the calibration spreadsheet once sweep finishes. @arjun @tess please review the PR for gating thresholds.

arjun: will review.

tess: reviewing — add an explicit check for generation truncation artifacts (e.g., premature EOS) in the full eval. we've seen quant moves that.

marta: noted, adding truncation check. will update the run when sweep completes. :sparkles:
